core_obligations: Record that a map of spaces is a homeomorphism exactly when it is injective, surjective and open (proof lines 5942-5944).
Conclude that a universal homeomorphism is the same as a morphism that is surjective, universally injective and universally open (proof lines 5944-5946).
Apply the three separate fpqc locality statements for those properties to obtain locality of the composite property (proof lines 5947-5950).
proof_roadmap: Splitting the property into three (proof lines 5944-5946).
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that the property of being a universal homeomorphism is fpqc local on the base (statement lines 5933-5937). The author first notes that the statement can be reduced to the corresponding statements for the three component properties, then supplies an explicit route: a map of topological spaces is a homeomorphism exactly when it is injective, surjective and open, so a universal homeomorphism is the same thing as a morphism that is at once surjective, universally injective and universally open, and locality on the base therefore follows from the three separate locality statements (proof lines 5939-5950). The claim is H2: the reduction to three already available locality results is written out, and the characterisation of homeomorphisms is stated rather than assumed.
